source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in a long leg cast cannot dorsiflex the foot. Which nerve is likely compressed?
questions.rationale: Pressure on the peroneal nerve causes footdrop.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Immobilized Extremities (PDF p. 451)
questions.quote: Injury to the peroneal nerve as a result of pressure is a cause of footdrop

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in a body spica cast has abdominal distention and vomiting. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Cast syndrome (superior mesenteric artery compression) causes ileus; NG decompression, IV fluids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spica Body Cast (PDF p. 451)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which action is outside the nurse's role for an external fixator?
questions.rationale: The nurse never adjusts clamps; that is the physician's responsibility.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, External Fixator (PDF p. 451)
questions.quote: The nurse never adjusts the clamps on the external fixator frame.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which solution is recommended for skeletal pin site care?
questions.rationale: Chlorhexidine is most effective; water is an alternative.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skeletal Traction (PDF p. 454)
questions.quote: Chlorhexidine solution is recommended as the most effective cleansing solution

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding shows traction is applied correctly?
options: Client slid to foot of bed
questions.rationale: Weights hang freely, ropes unobstructed, client centered, knots away from pulleys.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Traction Principles (PDF p. 452)
questions.quote: Weights must hang freely and should not rest on the bed or floor.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Removing weights from skeletal traction is allowed only:
questions.rationale: Skeletal traction is never interrupted except in emergencies.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skeletal Traction Alert (PDF p. 454)
questions.quote: The nurse must never remove weights from skeletal traction unless a life-threatening situation occurs

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Buck's extension traction is used for:
questions.rationale: Buck's is skin traction to the lower leg before hip or femur surgery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Traction (PDF p. 452)
questions.quote: Affectation of the hip and the femur

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in Buck's traction reports burning under the boot. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Burning may indicate nerve damage or skin breakdown.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Traction (PDF p. 452)
questions.quote: The nurse should immediately investigate any complaint of a burning sensation

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Bryant's traction is used for femur fractures in children younger than:
questions.rationale: Bryant's skin traction is for children under 3 (small weight).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Traction (PDF p. 452)
questions.quote: The Affectation of the hip and femur for children below 3 yrs. Old

questions.subject: NP III
questions.rationale: Crutchfield tongs are skeletal traction for cervical spine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skeletal Traction (PDF p. 453)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which exercise reduces venous stasis in a client in traction?
questions.rationale: Active ankle flexion-extension and calf pumping 10 times an hour.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skeletal Traction (PDF p. 454)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After total hip replacement, the leg should be kept in:
questions.rationale: Abduction pillow prevents dislocation; never flex hip over 90 degrees.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Total Hip Replacement (PDF p. 456)
questions.quote: Positioning the leg in abduction, which helps prevent dislocation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement shows understanding after hip replacement?
options: I'll use a raised toilet seat
questions.rationale: Raised seats limit hip flexion; avoid crossing legs and bending at waist.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Total Hip Replacement (PDF p. 456)
questions.quote: raised toilet seats are used to minimize hip joint flexion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Prophylactic antibiotics before joint replacement are most effective when given:
questions.rationale: Antibiotics within 60 minutes before incision prevent infection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Orthopedic Surgery (PDF p. 456)
questions.quote: Prophylactic antibiotic 60 minutes prior to incision

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After hip replacement, which drug class prevents DVT?
questions.rationale: Enoxaparin, fondaparinux, stockings, and early ambulation prevent DVT.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Total Hip Replacement (PDF p. 457)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A continuous passive motion device after knee replacement is used to:
questions.rationale: CPM increases circulation and knee range of motion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Total Knee Replacement (PDF p. 457)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The level of amputation is chosen as:
options: Most distal point that will heal
questions.rationale: Preserve length and function; based on circulation and prosthesis fit.
questions.quote: Most distal point that will heal successfully.
